headline: Conditions accepted for 2 New Bond Street school athletic fields, including artificial turf and anti-climb fencing.
summary: Conditions require a spec sheet for the turf product before construction, showing its PFAS content. They also require an operation and maintenance plan for the field and upkeep of the anti-climb fence. A project change for 315 and 317 Southwest Cutoff and an access path at 301 Barber Avenue were approved. Negative determinations were approved for Mill Street and 321 Greenwood Street, and a Certificate of Compliance for Curtis Apartments Phase 1 was approved.
decisions: Postponed the 413 Lake Avenue hearing to December 7th and withdrew the 80 Barber Avenue request, 4-0.
Accepted the conditions for 2 New Bond Street, 3-0.
Approved a negative determination for the Mill Street right of way request.
Approved a negative determination for 321 Greenwood Street.
Approved a Certificate of Compliance for Curtis Apartments Phase 1.
Approved a project change request for 315 and 317 Southwest Cutoff, with a changed stormwater design.
Approved a project change request to add an access path at 301 Barber Avenue.
Approved amending the enforcement order to require the restoration plan at 342 Lake Avenue.
Ratified the staff-issued enforcement order for 416 Belmont Street.
discussion: Turf field PFAS questions: Members asked why the term PFAS-free appeared in quotation marks. The applicant's sports field designer said trace amounts are far below state and federal limits, and a spec sheet will be required before construction.

301 Barber Avenue access path: Members asked how crews would remove collapsed wall material and whether the path would stay stable in spring. The applicant's wetland scientist said the path is compacted and stable, and erosion controls would be checked after winter.

215 Lake Avenue fence: Members said a fence would not be allowed in the 30-foot buffer along the water and noted wildlife movement. The prospective owner asked about a 4-foot fence for safety with a young son and a dog.

342 Lake Avenue pavement: Members said added pavement outside the no-disturbance zone could go through a project change request, subject to zoning review. Staff suggested a May 1st restoration deadline.

Wetlands ordinance changes: Staff said Sewers raised concerns about raising the ground disturbance threshold to 20,000 square feet. Staff may hold off on that recommendation and hopes to finish the changes by the December 7th meeting.
